calibration.rules: temperature by validation NLL; tau50 = 0.5 on the calibrated probability; tau85 = the highest threshold whose validation END recall is >= 0.85 (§7); neither ever from test

rules.metric: AUC on the conversation validation records cut at d = 0.2 s (§6.4)
rules.eligible: Smart Turn validation accuracy at tau 0.5, d = 0, f32 >= 0.88
rules.choice: the eligible from-v2 arm with the highest metric; P4 instead if eligible and higher by more than 0.005 (amendment 1: or the only eligible arm)
rules.stop: no eligible arm, or the chosen arm below v2's file on the same cuts + 0.01 (§6.5)

cuts_8_3.rule: spans of 0.2 s or more cut at start + 0.2 s, holds over 5 s ignored (§8.3); counted before any model reads them

crosscheck.about: docs/s6-ear3-prereg.md §3.7 as amended (amendment 2): every eligible energy record of the validation sessions labelled again at its instant from Silero VAD v6.2.3's speech runs, with the same label code. The bars: the agreement on every record whose instant label is not a drop, and the share of records whose instant label is a drop. The offset matching (within 150 ms, one to one) is reported and decides nothing. Silero selects, drops and relabels nothing.

bleed.about: docs/s6-ear3-prereg.md §3.7, the bleed probe: on the training records, the AUC (end of turn against hold) of the mean raw log10-energy channel of A's hops lying wholly in [o, o + d]

data.rule: docs/s6-ear3-prereg.md §3.2 (amendment 1): drops counted by the first rule that applies, in the order of item 5; sessions absent from splits.json are not decoded
data.class_ratio: amendment 2: the caps keep every eligible end-of-turn record and draw the holds up to the total, so the stored ratio is not the natural one; counts.eligible holds the natural counts by split, [hold, end of turn]

disclosure: **Disclosure (§11).** v3 was designed after v2's eot-bench reading: the overall, per-language and per-cohort numbers of runs/s6-ear2-nano/GATE.json were seen, and that reading motivated making eot-bench the headline, the no-harm bar outside English and the expected per-language effects. eot-bench has never been used for training or for any choice of v2's or v3's training: no eot-bench file was opened for v3's design, and the cut point (0.2 s) comes from the demo's policy and LiveKit's card, not from a reading. The variable trailing silence was motivated by the microphone demo (turn.ts), through the code. v3's study measured the trailing silence of 3,160 of v2's training clips. Smart Turn's test is still partly in-sample for the design, as v2's disclosure says; v3 adds no reading of it before the gate. The label cross-check and the caps were amended after a measurement on five training sessions, before any validation or test session was read (amendment 2: Silero's label read at each energy record's instant; every end-of-turn record kept). **What it means:** the training corpus is human-to-human and eot-bench is human-to-agent (the labels of the training conversations are the listener's behaviour, not an agent's need); the training conversations are English and eot-bench has 14 languages; the conversation test is session-disjoint, not speaker-disjoint.
meaning: E1 fails on its lower bound: no improvement on real human-to-agent speech is shown. Test (c) separates the causes: if (c) improves over v2, the human-to-human signal does not transfer to agents; if not, the model did not learn the signal.
sentence: Keep v2 (or take Smart Turn's 8.7 MB file when real conversations matter most): v3 does not pass; on eot-bench at the policy's first question (0.2 s into each pause) its AUC is 0.7197 against v2's 0.7448 (change -0.0252, 95% interval [-0.0336, -0.0167]) and Smart Turn's 0.7873; on Smart Turn's test clips its accuracy is 0.8978 against v2's 0.8993.
